summary.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q2 FY27: business up 25% YoY, advances up 30%, ROE 26.98%, GNPA down 47 bps to 1.25%.
summary.overview: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics were met in Q2, with business crossing INR7 lakh crore and advances growing 30% YoY (23% ex-IBU). Operating profit rose 31% and net profit 41% YoY, lifting ROE 440 bps to 26.98% and NIM 12 bps to 3.97%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.25% and NNPA at 0.12%, helped by write-off recoveries and lower NPA provisions, while INR500 crore of ECL provisions was booked in the standard asset line. Cost of deposits fell 4 bps YoY to 4.38%, though management acknowledged a QoQ rise tied to FCNR(B) and OFCB raises of about $1.65 billion.

financial_highlights.metric: Cost of deposits / cost of funds

segments.name: Advances / large credit
segments.commentary: Large credit up 38% YoY to INR36,000 crore, of which INR18,000 crore from GIFT City IBU and INR18,000 crore domestic (19% growth). Domestic credit ex-IBU grew 23%, with RAM, retail, agri and MSME each above 20%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Deposits up 22% YoY, or 19% ex-FCNR(B); CASA up 12% YoY with INR19,000 crore CASA added over the last FY.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri book INR44,000 crore, up 34% YoY (about INR11,000 crore). Agri gold loans INR18,600 crore vs INR6,500 crore in Sep-25; agri stress down 35 bps to 3.51%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Total gold loan outstanding INR33,000 crore; MSME gold loan about INR2,000 crore. Retail gold declined QoQ as loans were reclassified to agri/MSME under RBI norms.

guidance_outlook: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics across growth, profitability, asset quality and capital were met in H1.
Domestic credit guidance is 18%; management sees no challenge sustaining above 18% with INR23,000 crore pipeline and INR10,000 crore expected to be disbursed by March 2027.
Recovery target from written-off accounts of INR1,300-1,500 crore annually for the next 4-5 years; FY27 recovery so far INR1,023 crore.
ECL: total assessed requirement INR2,500 crore over 4 years; INR750 crore already provided (INR250 crore earlier plus INR500 crore in Q2), which management says covers more than 1 year.
Maharashtra debt-waiver government receivable (about INR2,700 crore of eligible INR3,500 crore): about INR1,200 crore received to 30 Sep; SLBC timeline for balance is 31 March 2027.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: about 200 branches planned annually; 77 branches made functional in H1 FY27.
Employee strength raised to 17,500 from about 13,000 two years earlier, driven by branch expansion and specialist hiring (treasury, IBU, IT).
IT budget: INR900 crore in FY25 and INR985 crore in FY26, with a large share on cyber security.
Pipeline sector mix: infra power about 18%, roads/HAM about 12%, renewables about 10%, metals and others about 10%; data centres cited as a niche growth area.
demand_pricing: Credit growth ex-IBU of 23% YoY; IBU book INR18,500 crore funded partly by about $560 million of FCNR(B) leverage. The FCNR(B) special window has closed.
Repricing: management raised rates on several MCLR-linked state PSU facilities (several thousand crore, about 25 bps on some) in Q1, contributing to NIM gains.
Global yield on advances 8.86%, domestic 9.02%; IBU yield not disclosed on the call.
Gold loan pricing tiers: agri lowest, MSME about 50 bps higher, non-priority retail highest.
EBLR-linked loans are 47% of the loan book.

qa_highlights.question: Provisioning: standard/restructured provisions rose to INR603 crore from INR76 crore; what is the ECL preparedness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NPA provisions fell from INR580 crore a year ago to INR120 crore this quarter, helped by recoveries. Standard-asset provisions rose to INR603 crore including INR500 crore of ECL; total ECL assessed at INR2,500 crore over 4 years, with INR750 crore already provided.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth sustain after the FCNR window closes, and will write-off recoveries continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IBU leverage was about $560 million from FCNR(B) and the window is closed; domestic growth is 23% and the INR23,000 crore pipeline supports growth above the 18% guidance. Write-off recovery target is INR1,300-1,500 crore a year for 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FCNR(B) is fixed at 6.51%, OFCB at 6.11%, and 1-year CDs at about 7.75-7.9%. About $1.65 billion was raised via FCNR(B) and OFCB against a $1.5 billion plan, with 5-year fixed-cost borrowings and a 3x oversubscribed MTN issue; YoY cost of deposits fell 4 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the 30 bps QoQ rise in yield on advances despite IBU mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to repricing of MCLR-linked state PSU accounts (about 25 bps on several thousand crore), a one-off write-off recovery impact of about 2-3 bps on NIM, and a 3-4 bps ITR refund. Only INR30 crore of the INR125 crore recovery has gone to interest income so far.

qa_highlights.question: Drought exposure and restructuring under SLBC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no visible agri stress; special SLBC restructuring applies at 33-50% crop loss (1-year moratorium, up to 3-year tenor) and above 50% loss (5-year tenor including 1-year moratorium). Farmer applications open till February 2027; past experience suggests 10-15% take-up, with about 5% provisioning on the restructured amount.

qa_highlights.question: Agri gold and retail gold trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri gold loans rose to INR18,600 crore from INR6,500 crore YoY. Retail gold declined QoQ because loans were reclassified to MSME/agri under RBI norms; total gold outstanding INR33,000 crore and MSME gold about INR2,000 crore.

risks_watch: Drought and El Nino: Maharashtra drought could trigger SLBC restructuring; management estimates 10-15% take-up and says no visible stress yet.
ECL transition: INR2,500 crore total assessed; management said the number may fall; surplus provisions of INR1,600-1,800 crore (COVID, global uncertainties INR200 crore) can be used.
Cost of deposits: QoQ increase from high-cost FCNR(B)/OFCB/CD raises; FY28 impact on margin depends on deployment.
Maharashtra debt-waiver balance of about INR1,500 crore receivable; management does not count on it and timing depends on state process (deadline 31 March 2027).
Pace of IBU growth after the FCNR(B) window closed; IBU yield not disclosed.
Cyber and DPDP compliance; management deferred detailed answer.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and profitability, with frequent emphasis on guidance delivery. Cautious on agri and drought stress, and evasive on IBU yield and October SMA data, which were deferred to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: And I'm happy to share that each one of those guidance numbers have been met, and this is getting consistently met also is one good feature.
So I don't see a challenge at all to maintain a pace above our guidance of 18% in credit in future also.
Our total assessment was that INR2,500 crores is our ECL provisioning to be done in 4 years.

growth.why: Domestic credit guidance of 18% for FY27 is backed by a INR23,000 crore pipeline with INR10,000 crore expected to be disbursed by March 2027, plus 77 branches opened in H1 against a plan of about 200 a year; the brief does not state a revenue growth figure for the quarter, and the 31% operating profit growth is the reported quarterly EBITDA-equivalent.
